turns.t: Come in, come in, and look at you, soaked through. Is it still pouring out there?
Oh, it's coming down in buckets. And the lot was full, so I had to park way down by the pharmacy.
Ugh, that's a trek when you're feeling poorly. Okay, let's get you sitting down. What brought you in today?
I've got this awful burning when I pee, and I just feel terrible all over.
I'm sorry. When did it start?
Monday. No, wait, Wednesday. It was Wednesday, because I'd just come home from my book club.
Okay, Wednesday. Is there anything else going on besides the burning?
I'm peeing all the time, practically every half hour, and I can't get comfortable.
Any pain anywhere? Your belly, your back?
A pain in my side. The left... no, sorry, the right side, down low by my back.
The right side, got it. Have you felt feverish or had chills?
I've been shivery since last night. Shaking under two blankets, and it's not even cold.
That sounds miserable. Any vomiting?
No, nothing like that.
Any blood in your urine?
No, I checked. Twice, actually. Or maybe three times.
Any diarrhea?
No diarrhea. My stomach is fine, apart from feeling generally awful.
Got it. Are you taking any medicines at the moment?
Just two. The metoprolol, 50 mg twice a day, and a vitamin D.
And what dose is the vitamin D, do you know?
1000 units, once a day. It says so right on the bottle, I just forgot to bring it.
That's helpful, thank you. Let's get your numbers. Nurse, could you take her vitals, please?
Sure thing. Arm up on the armrest for me, Mrs. Hadley.
All done, Doctor. I've put everything on the screen for you.
Thanks. Blood pressure is 118 over 72, pulse 104, temperature 38.4 degrees Celsius, breathing 18 breaths per minute, oxygen 97 percent.
Is that bad? I'm so foggy today I can barely follow.
The temperature and pulse are up, so your body's busy fighting something. May I press on your back, Mrs. Hadley?
Go ahead. Ow! Right there, yes.
There's tenderness over your right flank, just below the ribs.
It really hurts when you press. What does that mean?
It tells me this is more than a bladder problem. Most likely it's a urine infection that's moved up toward your kidney.
Oh dear. So what do we do?
First, I'd like a urine sample sent to the lab for culture. Can you manage that now?
I think so. I've been going every half hour, after all. Ha.
Hi, I'm Priya from the front desk. Here's the sample cup and the labeled bag. The restroom is down the hall to the left.
Left... or was it right? Sorry, I keep mixing them up today.
Left, just past the water fountain. I'll run it to the lab myself as soon as you bring it back.
Thank you, dear. I'll be right back.
Take your time. Nurse, once she's done, could you settle her in the treatment room with a blanket?
Of course. I'll bring a warm blanket and a glass of water for you, Mrs. Hadley.
Sip water steadily while you wait, as much as you comfortably can.
Will do. Thank you all, I feel better already just being looked after.
That's what we're here for. Rest up now.
